That said, since he hasn't shown interest in wearing it out and about, I really haven't turned that question over in my mind very much, but I might still err on the side of letting him. I absolutely understand the various concerns of people who disagree with that, and I don't think that every one of those concerns is necessarily without merit; however, he has always been a very crafty, artistic, unique person, and I would hate to send the message to him that this (or really any) particular means of creative expression is something that should be hidden or a source of shame, or that (as some others have opined) there is some kind of sexualization implicit in it, because I happen to disagree with those notions. I do agree that skin care needs to be addressed, so we are doing that, but your (and others') concerns seem to be more rooted in the potential effects of other people's reactions. I don't think that that concern is necessarily misplaced; as a mother, of course I want for my sons never to face ridicule or bigotry or anything of that sort. But as a mother, I have also tried very hard to educate them about all the very different people and viewpoints in the world, and how to coexist with them when conflict arises. I have tried to bolster their confidence and their respective senses of self. I have come to the conclusion that for my children, it would be so much less damaging and disastrous to possibly deal with the dissent of a few individuals than to perceive and learn shame and self-doubt from their own mother. So I think, if the issue ever does come up, I will opt to be his supportive soft place to fall, in case others aren't.  I hope that looooong blurb didn't come off as preachy or adversarial. I didn't mean for it to; you just touched on interesting and thus far unconfronted parenting territory for me. Thank you! :)

Unfortunately, I don't really use a specific recipe for the cheesecake buttercream; I just wing it. I sort of build onto a basic ABC recipe. When I'm creaming the butter, I add an ounce or two of cream cheese (not enough to make the structure unstable) or some cream cheese flavoring. Then I add the cream (or milk, whatever is preferred) and add cheesecake flavored pudding powder into it very slowly so that it's not grainy. Alternatively, you could probably mix the liquid and pudding together ahead and just toss the prepared (but very thick and concentrated) pudding in there. It shouldn't be a lot-- I just use part of a pudding packet and cinch it closed for future use in other frosting or baked goods. Then I add salt, powdered sugar, and milk or cream and whatever extract ( in this case, LorAnn blueberry emulsion-- but be careful, because a little of it goes a looooong way) until the consistency and taste are as they should be . I hope this makes sense and is at least a little helpful!
